title: Extensible Cross-Modal Hashing
motivation: Real-world cross-modal retrieval systems face continuously arriving new data categories; existing CMH methods lack extensibility and suffer catastrophic forgetting
problem_framing: Incremental learning problem: update hash function to support new categories using only new data while preserving performance on old tasks and old hash codes
key_insight: Agreement matrix identifies dimensions where cross-modal representations already agree; these dimensions should be frozen via weak constraint distillation, allowing selective update of disagreed dimensions
method_signature: ECMH with self-taught distillation loss + common space learning + hash function learning, using agreement matrix as dimension selector
evaluation_criteria: Mean Average Precision (MAP), Precision-Recall curves, training time cost comparison against retraining baseline
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Self-taught distillation slightly limits new task performance (up to 2.7% MAP decrease vs fine-tuning); trade-off accepted to preserve old knowledge
evidence_for_taste: A traditional fine-tuning method suffers the catastrophic forgetting effect
those method cannot resolve the cross-modal hashing problem
we adopt an alternating strategy to solve the non-convex objective
the hash code smoothing factor β helps prevent overfitting
thinking_moves: 把增量学习中的参数更新问题转化为'同意/不同意'维度选择问题
通过agreement matrix把hard constraint变成weak constraint来缓解灾难性遗忘
不追求new task的极致性能，而是寻求old和new task的平衡
